_comment: What the agent knows how to recognise when a run dies, and what each one
means for whoever gets the toast. This is a table rather than an
alternation inside a shell function so that adding a cause is a data
change, and so that something can enumerate what the agent can explain.
A failure matching nothing here is reported as 'unclassified' with its
own evidence line attached. That is the point: an unexplained failure has
to be visible as unexplained, not fall quietly into a default branch.
Patterns are extended regular expressions, matched case-insensitively
against the run log with grep -aoiE. Keep them anchored on wording the
backend actually printed, and keep the trailing {0,n} bounded so a match
cannot drag half a log into a desktop notification.

evidence_noise_prefixes: lines that exist in every run log before anything can fail. The task briefing is the trap: it lists open pull requests and issue titles, and one of those titles contained the word 'errors', so the audit reported a contributor's PR title as the reason a run died.
evidence_noise_patterns: the same job as the prefixes, for lines older log formats wrapped differently. A commit line from the briefing was being reported as the reason a run died.

evidence_starts_after: the task briefing lists open pull requests, issue titles and commit subjects, and any of those can contain the word 'error'. Nothing before the last of these markers is evidence of anything, so evidence selection starts after it. Chasing the briefing line by line with noise prefixes was losing that argument one string at a time.

transient.means: the next scheduled slot fixes this by running again

needs_human.means: no retry clears this and every later slot fails the same way

shapes.means: the model usage window is closed and reopens on a clock
the model usage window is closed and reopens on a clock
the provider is shedding load
the provider is rate limiting this account
the provider returned a server error
the connection to the provider broke mid-request

shapes.pattern: can'?t reach the api server.{0,60}|network is unreachable
shapes.means: this host could not reach the provider at all
the provider's name did not resolve

shapes.pattern: error connecting to api\.github\.com|could not reach github
shapes.means: GitHub was unreachable, so the run never verified its identity
the backend login has expired
the backend rejected the credential it was given
shapes.fix: claude /login, or fix the key in profile.env

shapes.pattern: your credit balance is too low.{0,60}
shapes.means: the backend account has no credit, and no retry pays an invoice
shapes.fix: top up the account, then: maintainer-doctor

shapes.means: the backend asked for an interactive login
the backend has no settings file deployed for this profile
the keyring's active GitHub account is not the one this profile posts as

shapes.pattern: could not pin a token for [A-Za-z0-9-]+
shapes.means: no token for this profile's account is in the keyring

shapes.pattern: refresh failed, no agent run started
shapes.means: the shared checkout could not be refreshed, usually a network or lock blip

shapes.pattern: another run held the lock for over [0-9]+s
shapes.means: a previous run was still holding the shared tree
something outside the run killed the process, so it never said why
the deployed tree has no doctrine file, so no run may start
the run started, wrote no diagnostic of its own, and stopped; the reason is outside the log
shapes._note: Never matched by pattern. _classify_log returns this id when a log holds the briefing and nothing else, and it is listed here so the taxonomy enumerates every id the agent can emit.

evidence_starts_after: run.sh closes the run for you
log renamed to match run id
